lemma_degree1.statement: Let F be a legitimate nonempty canonical unit-free root with n live variables, m clauses and L literal occurrences. If L<2n, then some live variable occurs exactly once.
proof: Every live variable occurs at least once, so the sum of occurrence counts is L and every count is a positive integer.
If every live variable occurred at least twice then L>=2n.
Therefore L<2n implies at least one variable has occurrence count exactly one.

lemma_degree1_elimination_reroot.statement: At an ordinary-elimination stage, eliminating a variable x that occurs exactly once creates no resolvents. If its unique clause C has width w>=2 and d>=1 live variables disappear after deleting C/canonicalizing, then the residual local input-size units N' satisfy N'<=N-(1+w+d)<=N-4.
proof: Because x occurs in exactly one polarity and one clause, one pivot bucket is empty, so pos*neg=0 and no resolvent is generated.
The raw residual is obtained by deleting the unique x-clause C; canonicalization and unit propagation can only delete more material.
Writing N=1+m+L+n and N'=1+m'+L'+n', we have m'<=m-1, L'<=L-w and n'=n-d with d>=1.
The ordinary stage is unit-free, so w>=2; therefore N'<=N-4.

cap_monotonicity.statement: The inherited N'<=24 theorem proves availability under the smaller local cap (N')^2. The actual frozen run retains the original cap 26^2, so every step certified under (N')^2 is also available under 26^2.

theorem.name: NO_RAW_CAP_RESCUE_REQUIRED_THROUGH_N26
theorem.statement: Combine the already-proved N<=25 corridor with the two only previously uncertified N26 root-count cells. In each N26 cell, L0<2r0 forces a degree-1 pivot. Exact elimination of that pivot generates no resolvents and re-roots the residual at local encoding size at most 22. The previously proved N<=24 ordinary-elimination corridor then completes raw-cap availability to the exact terminal lanes, under a cap no larger than the original 26^2 cap. Thus v2/v3 cannot be required because of ordinary raw-cap unavailability for any legitimate root with N<=26.
